OPS_065.context: After a meeting, two sets of minutes were circulated with different dates for the same milestone.
OPS_065.text: How will you restore a single plan?

options.A: I will check the meeting notes and the original grounds for the change of date.
options.B: I will contact the participants to confirm the common agreement.
options.C: I will check the source of the discrepancy and agree a single set of minutes with the teams.
options.D: I will suspend distribution of the schedule and arrange for the date to be clarified.

OPS_066.context: The contractor asks to remove a control milestone for system testing in order to make the report look good.

options.A: I will keep the milestone and propose a separate indicator for installation.
options.B: I will explain that the milestone reflects a mandatory result and will remain.
options.C: I will ask the contractor for a written justification of the change.
options.D: I will check the approved plan and the grounds for changing control points.

OPS_067.context: Actual material deliveries are on schedule, but unloading overlaps with concrete works.
OPS_067.text: How will you refine the schedule?

options.A: I will enter the agreed unloading windows into the operational plan.
options.B: I will note the conflict and ask the dispatcher to propose a time.
options.C: I will check the process constraints and available unloading areas.
options.D: I will check the work constraints and record a safe time slot in the plan.

OPS_068.context: At the weekly meeting, the technical department (PTO) engineer and the supervisor give different floor completion percentages.
OPS_068.text: How will you run the discussion?

options.A: I will record both values and schedule a check against the source data.
options.B: I will point out the dispute and propose that the team confirm the percentage with a walk-round.
options.C: I will organise a joint walk-round and a check of the completed areas.
options.D: I will confidently ask them to show the quantities and the readiness criterion.

OPS_069.context: The schedule has float, but it is being proposed for additional work that has not yet been approved.
OPS_069.text: How will you assess the decision?

options.A: I will check the impact on the critical path and the likelihood of approval.
options.B: I will warn about the risk of losing the float before the decision is made.
options.C: I will present a calculation of the float and propose an approval procedure with justification.
options.D: I will keep the float as a separate line until the change is confirmed.

OPS_070.context: The general contractor changed the order of floor handover, affecting the finishing and services schedules.
OPS_070.text: How will you update the plan?

options.A: I will formalise the change of order and recheck the transitions with the teams.
options.B: I will record the new sequence and the versions of the dependent schedules.
options.C: I will send the new sequence to the contractors and request comments.
options.D: I will bring together the supervisors of both disciplines to agree the available work areas.

OPS_071.context: The team rarely reports obstacles before the weekly report, and risks become visible too late.
OPS_071.text: How will you improve the reporting of problems?

options.A: I will agree a simple daily channel for reporting blockers with the supervisors.
options.B: I will add a blockers item to the daily operational report.
options.C: I will review cases where an early signal could have changed the decision.
options.D: I will identify typical causes of delay and, together with the team, introduce brief problem notifications.

OPS_072.context: Management asks for an exact completion date for the stage while a delivery is unconfirmed.
OPS_072.text: How will you word the forecast?

options.A: I will give a date from the current schedule with a note about the delivery risk.
options.B: I will openly present a range with a documented condition and a date for review.
options.C: I will record the assumption, the range of dates and the deadline for revising the forecast.
options.D: I will say the date is conditional and name its dependence on confirmation of the delivery.

OPS_073.context: In the coordination model, an air duct crosses a beam, and installation is scheduled for next week.
OPS_073.text: How will you clarify the route?

options.A: I will check the model elevations, the drawings and acceptable bypass options with the designer.
options.B: I will file a change request and stop the disputed section from being released for installation.
options.C: I will check the clash and submit the change through the agreed approval route.
options.D: I will mark the section as blocked and send a request to the coordinator.

OPS_074.context: HVAC (OViK) installers report that the ceiling void is taken up by cable trays.
OPS_074.text: How will you agree on the placement?

options.A: I will propose a joint walk-round and record the agreed elevations.
options.B: I will point out the need for a joint solution and a deadline before the ceiling is closed.
options.C: I will request current drawings from the adjacent trades and schedule a meeting.
options.D: I will bring together representatives of HVAC (OViK), electrical (EOM) and finishing to check the routes on site.

OPS_075.context: The data sheet of the delivered fan shows an airflow lower than the design value.
OPS_075.text: How will you assess the delivery?

options.A: I will tell procurement that an equivalent cannot be accepted without approval.
options.B: I will set the equipment aside for checking and send the data sheet to the designer.
options.C: I will compare the operating point, the unit's performance curve and the design calculation.
options.D: I will check the characteristics and, with justification, reject the unconfirmed substitute.

OPS_076.context: It is proposed to carry out ventilation tests before the network has been sealed.
OPS_076.text: How will you structure the order of work?

options.A: I will postpone the tests and ask the contractor to confirm the network is ready.
options.B: I will schedule a check of the sealing before the tests and agree the dates with the team.
options.C: I will agree a new sequence with the installers and the commissioning engineers.
options.D: I will record the readiness of the sections and the condition for starting the tests according to the programme.

OPS_077.context: The actual air exchange differs markedly between two rooms of the same purpose.
OPS_077.text: How will you organise the analysis?

options.A: I will compare the settings, the damper positions and the measurement results.
options.B: I will carry out a joint inspection with the commissioning engineers and operations.
options.C: I will check the reasons for the difference together with the commissioning engineers and agree an adjustment.
options.D: I will request the measurement reports and schedule a repeat check.

OPS_078.context: On site they want to replace the vibration mounts of the equipment without the supplier's calculation.

options.A: I will explain the risk and send the replacement for documented approval.
options.B: I will clearly state the need to confirm the parameters of the replacement.
options.C: I will keep the design mounts in the order until the designer replies.
options.D: I will check the specification and arrange technical approval.

OPS_079.context: The plumbing (VK) pipe route passes through a room whose layout has changed.
OPS_079.text: How will you clarify the position of the pipes?

options.A: I will formalise an agreed change to the route before installation.
options.B: I will suspend work in the section and send the drawing for interdisciplinary review.
options.C: I will check the current architectural layout, the elevations and the connection points.
options.D: I will check the clashes and record the new route in the working documents.

OPS_080.context: Installers found that access to a drainage inspection point is blocked by built-in furniture.
OPS_080.text: How will you settle the matter with the adjacent trades?

options.A: I will request the current furniture layout and arrange coordination.
options.B: I will state the access requirement and agree the detail with the adjacent trades.
options.C: I will bring together the finishers, the architect and the plumbing (VK) crew to choose an access location.
options.D: I will openly explain why access to the inspection point must be kept.

OPS_081.context: Water pipe pressure-test results differ between two instruments.
OPS_081.text: How will you interpret the test?

options.A: I will check the condition of the instruments, the method and the test record.
options.B: I will state that the result cannot yet be considered confirmed.
options.C: I will arrange a repeat test using the agreed method and explain the reason.
options.D: I will request metrological verification of the instruments and a repeat measurement with those responsible.

OPS_082.context: The plumbing (VK) joints are already boxed in, but the as-built drawing does not show part of the concealed route.
OPS_082.text: How will you organise restoring the data?

options.A: I will restore the drawing with the contractors and formalise confirmation of the actual route.
options.B: I will note that the documentation is incomplete and request supporting materials.
options.C: I will register the gap and pass it to the responsible plumbing (VK) engineer.
options.D: I will gather the installer, the technical department (PTO) and quality control to restore the route.

OPS_083.context: The contractor reports occasional pump noise at start-up, although the data sheet figures are normal.
OPS_083.text: How will you look for the cause?

options.A: I will discuss the observations with the commissioning engineers and operations.
options.B: I will request the start-up log and schedule a check of the installation.
options.C: I will compare the operating modes, the piping, the mountings and the start-up records.
options.D: I will carry out a joint inspection of the modes and record verifiable hypotheses.

OPS_084.context: Procurement offers a pump from stock with a different connection size.
OPS_084.text: How will you agree the solution?

options.A: I will keep the original item until the designer gives an opinion.
options.B: I will state the conditions for the substitution and send the comparison for approval.
options.C: I will check the parameters and formalise technical approval of the equivalent.
options.D: I will report that the substitution requires checking the scheme and the connection.

OPS_085.context: On the electrical (EOM) plan, a cable route passes through a recently added fire protection detail.
OPS_085.text: How will you check the change?

options.A: I will check the current drawings, the purpose of the assembly and acceptable bypass paths.
options.B: I will prepare an interdisciplinary request and a new revision of the route.
options.C: I will check the assembly's constraints and agree a documented bypass.
options.D: I will mark the route as conflicting and stop installation of this segment.

OPS_086.context: Electricians and low-current installers both want the same spot for panels in the corridor.
OPS_086.text: How will you agree the layout?

options.A: I will present the constraints of both panels and agree the placement together.
options.B: I will clearly state the need for agreed access for maintenance.
options.C: I will request the dimensions and access zones from both teams.
options.D: I will organise a joint measurement of the corridor and a meeting with the designer.

OPS_087.context: During cable labelling, some tags do not match the current single-line diagram.
OPS_087.text: How will you find the cause?

options.A: I will state that connecting the disputed lines before a check is unacceptable.
options.B: I will isolate the disputed items from commissioning work and notify the electrician.
options.C: I will check the circuit numbers, the diagram revisions and the actual connections with an authorised specialist.
options.D: I will organise a check of the circuits and secure corrected labelling.

OPS_088.context: Commissioning of a panel is scheduled before the check of the protective bonding is complete.
OPS_088.text: How will you change the plan?

options.A: I will mark the panel as not ready and request the test report.
options.B: I will formalise the dependency and move the start-up to a verified date together with the team.
options.C: I will agree an available window for the check with the testers and the installers.
options.D: I will make confirmation of the check a condition for starting up.

OPS_089.context: On the floor, socket positions are regularly changed after the installation drawings are issued.

options.A: I will find out at what stage of approval the new requirements appear.
options.B: I will hold a meeting of the electrical (EOM) and architectural teams and the future users of the rooms.
options.C: I will identify the source of the changes and agree a joint check before release.
options.D: I will propose obtaining confirmation of the furniture layout before installation.

OPS_090.context: Installers propose connecting a temporary load to a free line without a verified calculation.

options.A: I will explain the restriction and arrange a check with a formal decision.
options.B: I will clearly refuse the connection until the line has been assessed by the responsible electrician.
options.C: I will pass the request to the person responsible for the electrical installation and leave the line disconnected.
options.D: I will check the design, the protection and the permitted procedure for a temporary connection.

OPS_091.context: During an interdisciplinary walk-round, different elevations were found in the HVAC (OViK) and plumbing (VK) drawings.
OPS_091.text: How will you determine the working elevation?

options.A: I will record the clash and release only an agreed solution for installation.
options.B: I will request a joint review and stop work in the disputed section.
options.C: I will check the revisions, the coordinates and the required falls with both disciplines.
options.D: I will check the source data and formalise an agreed elevation before installation.

OPS_092.context: When a plant room is handed over, operations asks for additional access to the valves and panels.
OPS_092.text: How will you handle the remark?

options.A: I will record the remark and schedule a joint walk-round of the room.
options.B: I will accept the remark and agree the location of the hatches with the adjacent trades.
options.C: I will gather operations, the installers and the architect for an on-site inspection.
options.D: I will point out the need to check access before the room is closed up.

OPS_093.context: After the tests a disagreement arose: the contractor considers the system ready, while operations is waiting for the reports.
OPS_093.text: How will you word the status?

options.A: I will separate the actual test result from the completeness of the document handover.
options.B: I will tell both sides directly that readiness for handover has not yet been confirmed.
options.C: I will check the missing reports and, with justification, indicate a conditional status.
options.D: I will draw up a list of documents and set a date for repeat handover.

OPS_094.context: Commissioning engineers do not see the pump alarm signal in the building management system, although the pump is running.
OPS_094.text: How will you organise the check?

options.A: I will document the open test item and agree a joint check of the circuit and logic.
options.B: I will record the mismatch in the test programme and not close the item until the signal is confirmed.
options.C: I will pass the remark to the commissioning engineers and schedule a repeat test of the signal.
options.D: I will bring together plumbing (VK), controls and electrical (EOM) specialists to check the signal chain.

OPS_095.context: During inspection of utility penetrations, sections were found without legible marking of the completed joint.
OPS_095.text: How will you prepare them for acceptance?

options.A: I will ask the installers and quality control to work together to restore the links identifying the joints.
options.B: I will draw up a list of unidentified places and schedule a joint inspection.
options.C: I will check each penetration against the design detail and the as-built schedule.
options.D: I will check the documents and, with the team, label the confirmed penetrations.
